extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent prosecutors, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, rejecting, and resolving double patenting issues (statutory and nonstatutory) between patents, pending applications, published applications, and reissue/reexamination matters under MPEP §804. Focuses on claim comparison, ownership/commonality, provisional rejections, terminal disclaimers, patent term dates, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the double patenting doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of double patenting seeks to prevent the unjustified extension of patent exclusivity beyond the term of a patent. The public should be able to act on the assumption that upon the expiration of the patent it will be free to use not only the invention claimed in the patent but also modifications or variants which would have been obvious to those of ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting results when the right to exclude granted in one patent is unjustly extended by the grant of another patent or patents. The focus of analysis is on whether grant of a second patent would give rise to an unjustified extension of rights; examine claims for scope and obvious variants. Citations: In re Zickendraht; In re Van Ornum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commonality requirement before raising double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commonality of inventorship or (deemed) ownership must exist between two or more patents or applications before consideration can be given to the issue of double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonality examples: same inventive entity, at least one common (joint) inventor (including sole vs joint naming situations), common applicant, common owner/assignee, or subject to a joint research agreement as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 102(c) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2) and (3). See 35 U.S.C. 100(f) and (g) definitions for inventor/joint inventor. If commonality does not exist, double patenting generally not applicable; consult MPEP §804.03 for non-common ownership/ joint research agreement situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two types of double patenting rejections (statutory and nonstatutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two general types of double patenting rejections: (1) the 'same invention' type (statutory) double patenting rejection based on the statutory language that an inventor may obtain a patent; and (2) the 'nonstatutory' (obviousness-type) double patenting rejection, a judicially created doctrine intended to prevent prolongation of patent term by prohibiting claims in a second patent not patentably distinct from claims in a first patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory double patenting is about claim identity/coextensiveness; nonstatutory focuses on patentable distinctness (obvious variants). Nonstatutory also addresses equitable concerns and risk of multiple suits by different assignees. Examiner must analyze claims to determine which type applies and apply appropriate remedies (statutory cannot be obviated by terminal disclaimer; nonstatutory can often be obviated by terminal disclaimer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-centered analysis (focus on claims for double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of any double patenting analysis necessarily is on the claims in the multiple patents or patent applications involved in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare scope of the claims (identity, coextensiveness, patentable distinctness). Nonstatutory double patenting can be based on anticipation, a one-way obviousness determination, or a two-way obviousness determination. The obviousness-type analysis is similar to but not necessarily the same as that under 35 U.S.C. 103. See In re Braat; In re Longi; Geneva Pharmaceuticals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior-art status and transition (FTI vs AIA) in charted analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing conflicting claims, examiners must consider whether the earlier reference (application or patent) is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 (FTI) or AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103, and use the appropriate chart versions (I-A_FTI, I-B_FTI, II-A_FTI, II-B_FTI versus I-A_AIA, I-B_AIA, II-A_AIA, II-B_AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In transition cases, an earlier-filed application may require use of FTI version for one application and AIA version for the other; consult MPEP §2159.03 to determine transition status. Determine if earlier-filed application or patent is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) or AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) before making anticipation/obviousness rejections. Consider exceptions under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A)/(B) for inventor-originated disclosures; case-by-case analysis required to establish inventor-originated disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting rejections (when allowed and how to use them)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may make a provisional double patenting rejection (statutory or nonstatutory) against a pending application when aware of copending applications or published applications that claim conflicting or indistinct inventions, provided confidential status and other statutory constraints are respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejections are used to notify applicant of potential problems if one application becomes a patent; they may be maintained until obviated. Published applications unredacted may be used; unpublished or redacted published applications may be used only when there is at least one common inventor/applicant/assignee or deemed common ownership per 35 U.S.C. 102(c) or pre‑AIA 103(c)(2). Replies to provisional rejections must overcome them by showing patentable distinctness or filing a terminal disclaimer; such replies should not be held in abeyance. See MPEP §§2136.01, 2154.01(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required responses to provisional nonstatutory double patenting (NSDP) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete response to a provisional NSDP rejection is either a reply showing that the claims subject to the rejection are patentably distinct from the reference claims, or filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c) or (d) with the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a response is required even when the NSDP rejection is provisional. Terminal disclaimers or a showing of patentable distinctness should not be held in abeyance; an application must not be allowed unless compliant terminal disclaimer(s) is/are filed and/or the rejection withdrawn by the examiner. See MPEP §1490 and §804.02 subsection VI for filing terminal disclaimers for applications filed on or after June 8, 1995.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements and effect for nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer, submitted in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321(c) or (d) to overcome a double patenting rejection, includes a provision that the patent is only enforceable for and during such period that it is owned by the same party (or parties) that owns the other patents or applications identified in the terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer establishes common ownership/enforceability limitation and can obviate nonstatutory double patenting rejections. Filing must be compliant; examiner should require proper terminal disclaimer when appropriate. Terminal disclaimers cannot overcome statutory double patenting rejections. See MPEP §1490 and form paragraph guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-application terminal disclaimer filing in multi‑app conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple applications conflict such that provisional NSDP rejections are made in each application, it is not sufficient to file a terminal disclaimer in only one application; an appropriate terminal disclaimer must be filed in at least two of the applications (and sometimes in each) to require common ownership or enforcement for all involved applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In three-application conflicts, filing in only one is insufficient; filing in two may be required, and in certain situations a terminal disclaimer may be required in each application. See MPEP §1490 subsection VI.D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term filing date determination for double patenting (utility and plant patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility and plant patents issuing on applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, the patent term ends on the date 20 years from the date on which the application was filed in the United States, or if the application contains a specific reference to one or more earlier-filed application(s) under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), 20 years from the filing date of the earliest such application (the 'patent term filing date').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term filing date is the earliest of: (1) the actual filing date; or (2) the filing date of the earliest application for which benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) is properly claimed. Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and foreign priority claims are not taken into account for patent term calculation. For reissue applications, the patent term filing date is that of the original application. See 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP §2701 and §211.01 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when provisional NSDP is the only remaining rejection (earlier/same/later patent term filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional NSDP rejection is the only rejection remaining, the examiner's action depends on whether the application under examination has an earlier, the same, or a later patent term filing date than the reference application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application under exam has earlier patent term filing date: withdraw the provisional rejection in earlier app and permit it to issue, converting the provisional rejection in the later app(s) into a nonstatutory double patenting rejection upon issuance. If same patent term filing date: maintain provisional NSDP until overcome (applicant may reply with patentable distinctness arguments or file a terminal disclaimer). If later patent term filing date: maintain the rejection until applicant overcomes it. If PTAB decision reversed other grounds but did not reach provisional NSDP and applicant hasn't filed terminal disclaimer, examiner must act (re-issue as nonprovisional rejection if reference issued as patent) or withdraw if reference abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory double patenting rejection and permitted responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory double patenting rejection (same invention) is overcome by canceling or amending the conflicting claims so they are no longer coextensive in scope, or by a reply showing the claims are not the same as the reference claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer cannot be filed to obviate a statutory double patenting rejection. A complete response must point out specific distinctions, amend claims, or cancel conflicting claims. Provisional statutory DP rejections follow similar examiner actions with regard to patent term filing dates as nonstatutory provisional rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application special rules for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications, patent term is measured from the issue date, so the patent term filing date determination used for utility/plant applications is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a provisional DP rejection (statutory or nonstatutory) is the only rejection remaining in the earlier filed of two conflicting design applications, withdraw the rejection in the earlier application and permit it to issue; maintain the provisional rejection in the later-filed application which will convert into a DP rejection upon issuance of the earlier application (unless obviated). For mixed design & utility/plant comparisons, consult TQAS or SPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting issues involving published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting may exist where a published patent application and an application share common inventive entity, applicant, owner/assignee, or are subject to joint research agreements; examiners may make provisional rejections when the published application has not issued and has not been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published application unredacted under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) can be used as DP reference without violating confidentiality. Redacted or unpublished applications can be used only with requisite commonality/deemed ownership. See handling of provisional rejections in subsection B for responses and maintenance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting in reissue and reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting issue may arise in reissue or reexamination between claims being reexamined and the claims of one or more applications and/or patents; it is necessary to determine whether the patents are subject to double patenting considerations in that context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP §2258 for double patenting rejections in reexamination proceedings. Determine ownership/commonality and claim relationships, and apply statutory vs nonstatutory analyses as appropriate. Consider whether terminal disclaimer or amendments are available remedies depending on statutory vs nonstatutory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 121 protection (restriction/divisional) limiting nonstatutory double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claimed invention that was the subject of a restriction requirement in one application is presented in a divisional application, a nonstatutory double patenting rejection cannot be applied to that claimed invention unless the restriction requirement was withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 121 shields claims against a double patenting challenge if consonance exists between the divided groups of claims and an earlier restriction requirement; if restriction requirement does not clearly set the line of demarcation or consonance is lost, Section 121 may not apply. If multiple patents result from an examiner's restriction requirement, Section 121 insulates resulting patents from nonstatutory double patenting rejection. See Geneva Pharmaceuticals v. GlaxoSmithKline; Applied Materials v. Advanced Semiconductor; see MPEP §804.01 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Technology Center Director for NSDP relying on parent in divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Office action containing a rejection on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting which relies on the parent application to reject claims in a divisional filed because of a restriction requirement under 35 U.S.C. 121 must be submitted to the Technology Center Director for approval prior to mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director disapproves the rejection, it shall not be mailed and other appropriate action taken. When the invention was the subject of a restriction requirement, a NSDP rejection cannot be applied to that claimed invention unless the restriction requirement was withdrawn. See MPEP §804.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Patent Term Extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. 156 on nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory double patenting does not invalidate any patent term extension granted under 35 U.S.C. 156, provided the claims are otherwise valid under the pre-PTE expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent, under its original expiration date without a PTE, should have been terminally disclaimed because of obviousness-type double patenting, then usual NSDP principles apply and the patent could be invalidated. However, if the patent is valid under pre-PTE expiration date, it is entitled to the full PTE. See Novartis AG v. Ezra Ventures LLC for court precedent. Examiner should apply these principles when PTE creates potential NSDP issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural handling of provisional DP after PTAB decisions or reference status changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PTAB decision does not reach a provisional NSDP rejection but reverses all other grounds for a claim and applicant has not filed a proper terminal disclaimer, the examiner must determine whether any reference application used in the provisional NSDP has issued as a patent and act accordingly (re-issue as nonprovisional DP rejection if reference issued; withdraw if reference abandoned or not matured).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should re-issue provisional rejections as nonprovisional where appropriate and may make them final if otherwise proper. If reference abandoned and no other grounds remain, withdraw the provisional rejection. See subsection I.B.1(iv) and MPEP §1214.06.
